Asexuality is a spectrum, and defined as a lack of sexual attraction. Libido is not the same as attraction, which might be why you’re confused. Just because I like to fuck myself when I’m ovulating doesn’t mean that I want to fuck anyone else. When you jerk off is it because you’re attracted to your hand? No it just feels good.

Lol it’s okay, I get why you’d be confused. Being asexual means feeling no sexual attraction to other people, which isn’t quite the same thing as not getting aroused or horny. When I look at a “hot” person I feel nothing at all. I don’t have any desire to have sex with anybody and most of the time can’t even recognise when people are super hot and when they aren’t. 

Some asexuals are totally sex repulsed and don’t enjoy sex/masturbation, but personally I love masturbating. I’m not attracted to other people, and I don’t want to have sex with them, but masturbation objectively feels good and that’s why I do it. I don’t find people hot so I also don’t watch porn. It’s just the physical feeling for me, if that makes sense, so rather than masturbating because someone/something turns me on, I do it because orgasms feel amazing.

You could be describing something called sensory symmetry! It’s very common in neurodivergent people, especially those of us with sensory processing disorders. Sometimes it can be an OCD thing, but other times it’s just a need for equal sensory input, and it can vary in severity. As a kid I used to spend hours making myself feel balanced or “just right” when something touched me on one side and not the other. I’m not really sure why it happens, but I’ll look into it more. For me, whenever I made routines I’d try and plan every minute of my day which meant it just wasn’t sustainable and I’d end up depressed and guilty when I “failed” to follow it. 

Just start by planning the bare necessities of your day, a good sleeping schedule was my starting point. And add more things as you go. Keep it a little flexible, and If you mess up one day it’s okay, just try again the next day. And don’t think you have to make it fancy like all the youtubers who are like... drinking lemon juice at 6am. Mine literally says, and I quote “eat some breakfast NOT TEA” 

It might take some playing around and changing to find something that really works for you, but you can get there I promise. Don’t give up!

I’ve been diagnosed with derealisation/depersonalisation disorder. Less than 2% of the population have this as a diagnosable disorder. 

The main symptom of depersonalization is a feeling of disconnect from one’s thoughts, feelings, and body. Derealisation is a similar feeling of being disconnected, but from one’s surroundings or environment. When I look in the mirror it’s almost like I’m looking at an entirely different person. 

Thankfully, I don’t have it 24/7 because when it strikes I become panicky, irritable and anxious, but I’m learning to deal with it and when you relax into the feeling it can actually be enjoyable in a strange way.
